newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chairman says Bull may seek alliance.
newsitem.headline: Chairman says Bull may seek alliance.

text.p: Cie des Machines Bull, the computer group in which the French state is in the process of reducing its stake to 17 percent, sees a next step in its development in a capital increase with an alliance.
Chairman Jean-Marie Descarpentries told the Le Journal des Finances weekly, to be published on Saturday, that a capital increase was a possibility.
Asked about the "next step" in the company's restructuring, Descarpentries said "That could be a capital increase coupled with a strategic move."
"This strategic move, we will pay it either with debt or with shares. But beware, a strategic move is not necessarily an acquisition," he said.
"It could be a joint-venture at 50/50, a partnership at 40/60 or 60/40 or an operation through one of our subsidiaries," Descarpentries said.
Asked whether Bull was looking at Olivetti or Siemens-Nixdorf, he said "Why are you only talking about Olivetti and Siemens-Nixdorf...".
The institutional sale of shares in Bull closed on Wednesday and was "greatly oversubscribed" according to the company.
France Telecom has an 18.7 percent stake while NEC Corp and Motorola Inc have similar stakes.
